title: Relabel if-expression label matching is slow: per-label canonicalization in the hot match loop

source.license_note: Real upstream victoria optimization PR #6432; measured-speedup task.

task.summary: Speed up labelFilter.equalValue matching in lib/promrelabel: avoid canonicalizing every label name on each iteration and add a fast path for bare __name__ (metric-name only) matches.
task.instructions: Optimize the lib/promrelabel package for speed WITHOUT changing behavior. The benchmark BenchmarkIfExpression measures it; existing tests must still pass.
task.acceptance_notes: Behavior preserved (go test passes); higher measured speedup is better. Do NOT edit any *_test.go.

code_fault.description: labelFilter.equalValue calls toCanonicalLabelName(label.Name) for every label in its match loop and has no fast path for bare metric-name (__name__) matching.

ops_fault.description: CPU profile of stream-aggregation/relabel ingestion shows hot time in promrelabel label filter matching during sample filtering.
detection_keywords: high CPU in hot match loop
hot path on every received sample
repair_keywords: add equalNameValue fast path for empty lf.label
avoid per-iteration canonicalization in hot loop

visible_context.issue_text: Under high ingestion, stream-aggregation and relabel filtering spend a disproportionate amount of CPU matching if-expressions against incoming samples, especially when the match selects only by metric name.
error_logs: pprof cpu: 31.4% lib/promrelabel.(*labelFilter).equalValue -> toCanonicalLabelName (alloc/normalize per label)
visible_context.notes: Real upstream optimization; profiling diagnosis injected as upstream context.
